title: You are the flea in the mayonnaise jar (GENETICS RANT)
summary: Using the flea-in-a-jar and five-monkeys experiments, he argues that belief in genetic limits is an artificial ceiling imposed by the YouTube fitness environment and propagated by viewers themselves. Genetic limits exist only because people believe in them; the solution is to leave the toxic environment and take individual responsibility.
claims: Belief in bad genetics is the most prevalent self-limiting belief in YouTube fitness and grows stronger every year
Motivational platitudes lose to arguments about DNA, so lifters need logical arguments against genetic pessimism; this builds on his earlier 'Schrodinger's genetics' concept
YouTube fitness is an environment in which creators and viewers shape each other in a feedback loop; many viewers' goals are borrowed from creators rather than their own
Some fitness doxa is valid, like progressive overload, but genetics is a harmful accepted belief
Successful fitness YouTubers suffer survivorship bias and, worshipped by viewers, come to believe they are genetically special
Flea experiment: fleas in a lidded jar learn to jump only below the lid and keep doing so after it is removed, and their offspring do the same; viewers are fleas and influencers placed the lid
Claims like 'you'll hit your limit in two years' or 'you must be gifted for 16-inch arms' come from YouTubers' anecdotes, not science
People accept artificial limits because of authority, because humans are prone to believing in limits, and because limits supply excuses (e.g. 'you can only reach 260 lb naturally')
Fitness YouTubers are not special; they have only more time training and the willingness to film themselves
Genetic limits exist only because you believe in them
Telling someone they have bad genetics brands them with a sentence they think they can never change, and they revolt when told the real problem is their training
Genetics is expressed potential; if you never train properly you can't know your potential, yet many quit before even a year of training

Five-monkeys experiment: monkeys sprayed for reaching bananas start beating any monkey that tries, and replacements who were never sprayed keep enforcing the rule; the cold spray is ridicule from influencers and peers
Words precede actions: ridicule makes people stop even voicing big goals, which prevents ever acting on them
Influencers plant artificial goals and steer lifters toward supplements, programs and coaching plans where profit lies, punishing deviating goals
Spreading genetics talk to others creates a crabs-in-a-bucket culture where anyone with ambition gets attacked; doing this to someone is your worst sin
The blackpill spreads like a contagion on YouTube and forums without needing active agents, and its believers can't explain why they believe it
DNA exists and people are gifted at different things, but no person on Earth lacks the ability to build a good physique
The real punishment is inaction; you choose to stay in the environment, so leave blackpill forums and stop consuming the poison
Influencers need viewers more than viewers need them; withdrawing approval removes their power to push toxic beliefs
